cases.name: Katherine Elizabeth Sinclair
cases.about: She was was enrolled in nursing school at Meridian Community College. Her mother said, "She loved to fish. That was her whole, entire world."  Her obituary said, "Katherine had numerous friends and enjoyed the simple life at Lake Eddins, where she oftentimes stated, “There is no place I’d rather be.” She was an avid fisherman and loved boating on the lake. She also loved music with a special affinity to classic rock. She loved life. Katherine’s death is a tragic one that is devastating to the family. There is a bright ray of sunshine and peace, as Katherine will live on as she has shared her organs so that others may celebrate their lives with their families."
cases.narrative:
Police found her shot in the head, gasping for breath, holding a gun in her right hand (she was left-handed) and naked from the waist down in the driver’s seat of her car in the driver’s seat in the garage of Burroughs’ home in the gated community of Windermere. Burroughs twice called Laurel Municipal Judge Kyle Robertson — his best friend and Sinclair’s uncle — before dialing 911 as she gasped for air in the car. She was pronounced dead at Forrest General Hospital the next day. The gun (Ruger LCP2 .380) was a gift to Sinclair from her father on May 19, her 23rd birthday. Despite being predominately left handed, Sinclair also could shoot with her right hand, Herrington said. "She always carried a gun with her at all times. It was always in her console," she said.
